instructions:
## Research objective

Your goal is to design reasoning and prompt engineering techniques to maximize algorithmic creativity (coherence, originality, diversity) on minimal open-ended algorithmic tasks inspired by combinational and exploratory creativity, and to assess limits of next-token prediction vs multi-token and diffusion approaches.

## Plan Formulation

- Reproduce four minimal tasks: Sibling Discovery, Triangle Discovery, Circle Construction, Line Construction, as defined by the paper’s coherence functions and uniqueness/originality criteria.
- Implement two core training paradigms on Transformers: next-token prediction (NTP; teacher forcing) and multi-token teacherless training (MTP; predict all response tokens in parallel given a prompt and dummy response inputs).
- Include a discrete diffusion baseline using SEDD (score-entropy discrete diffusion) with absorb variant, comparable in non-embedding parameter count to a small Transformer.
- Systematically compare randomness elicitation methods: temperature + (optionally) top-k/top-p sampling at output vs seed-conditioning (random input prefixes) with deterministic decoding.
- Primary metrics: algorithmic creativity ˆcrN = fraction of generated samples that are coherent, unique, and not in training; plus component metrics: coherence rate, diversity (uniq/|T|), and memorization rate.
- Run controlled ablations: seed length, sampling temperature, top-k on/off, task token ordering (notably reverse order for Sibling Discovery), dataset size, task complexity (graph degree/triangle density; circle/line sizes), and model size.
- Optional extension: summarization (XSUM, CNN/DailyMail) to study diversity-quality tradeoffs via Self-BLEU vs ROUGE under NTP vs MTP and with/without seed-conditioning.
- Target replications of headline results: MTP and diffusion improve algorithmic creativity over NTP; seed-conditioning induces diversity comparable to temperature and sometimes better; MTP reduces memorization, seed-conditioning boosts diversity.

## Data Preparation

- General conventions: tokenize vertices/entities as simple ASCII tokens (e.g., single lowercase letters or integer IDs), separate tokens with spaces, and format edges as 'u→v' pairs separated by commas. Use uppercase A,B,C,... for parents; lowercase a,b,c,... for children; or integer IDs for large graphs.
- Seed-conditioning pretexts: during training, prepend each example with a seed string: 'SEED: <S>' where <S> is a random uppercase string of length L∈{0,2,4,10}. Also prepare 'null' (no seed) and 'pause' prefixes (e.g., 10 special [PAUSE] tokens) for controls.
- Sibling Discovery data: • Construct a bipartite in-weights graph with |V_parents|=5 and |children per parent|=500 (default). • Training samples are triplets in sibling-first order: '(γ, γ′, Γ)' where γ,γ′∈nbr(Γ). Ensure training size S satisfies S ≈ O(m·n) but S << O(m·n^2) (e.g., 50k). • Do not provide the graph in-context; the model must infer edges from samples. • For reverse-order ablation, also prepare '(Γ, γ, γ′)' data.
- Triangle Discovery data: • Build an undirected graph G(V,E) with |V|=999, target average degree deg≈3, and per-vertex triangles tri≈6. Enforce max degree ≤1.2·deg and add explicit neighbor-neighbor edges to reach target triangles. • Training set: 2/3 edges and 1/3 triangles. Mark with prefixes 'edge:' and 'tri:'. • Represent a triangle as 'tri: (u,v),(v,w),(w,u)' and edges as 'edge: (u,v),(v,u)' to mitigate reversal issues. • Training size ≈ 15k.
- Circle Construction data: • Choose graph size N=9 edges and vocabulary size M=15 distinct vertex tokens (M>N). • Samples are shuffled adjacency lists that resolve to a single N-cycle under some permutation π: 'a→b, c→d, ...' with N edges. Training size ≈ 10k.
- Line Construction data: • Same as Circle but sequences resolve to a line (path) of length N: 'v1→v2, v2→v3, ..., vN-1→vN'. Training size ≈ 10k; defaults N=9, M=15.
- Uniqueness/originality canonicalization: • Sibling: canonical key is the literal '(γ,γ′,Γ)' string; train set membership is exact set membership. • Triangle: canonicalize by triangle identity; treat permutations as identical. Use a sorted triple of vertex IDs (or lexicographically minimal rotation) as key; declare mem if triangle appears in training triangles (ignoring permutation). • Circle/Line: uniqueness is over resolving permutations, invariant to vertex renaming. Build a graph from the edge list, verify it resolves to a single simple cycle/line; relabel vertices by first-appearance order and derive a normalized permutation signature (e.g., for cycles, the smaller of forward/backward rotations starting at index 0). Deduplicate and check train mem by these signatures.
- Generation sets: • For each condition, generate T ≥ 1024 independent samples per checkpoint with new random seeds (for seed-conditioning) and record all metadata needed for later analysis (prefix type/length, sampling params). Ensure separation of train and eval seeds.

## Running Experiments

- Models: • Large Transformer: Gemma v1 2B (or similar open model) for main trends. • Small Transformer: GPT-2 (≈86M non-embedding params) for parity with diffusion. • Diffusion: SEDD (≈90M non-embedding params), absorb variant, 128 denoising steps.
- Training objectives: • NTP (teacher forcing): standard next-token loss over response tokens given prompt+gold prefix. • Teacherless MTP: predict all response tokens ri in parallel given the prompt and a dummy response input (e.g., a sequence of $ tokens). Blend losses if desired: total_loss = λ·MTP + (1−λ)·NTP with λ∈{0.25,0.5,0.75}.
- Seed-conditioning: • Training: prepend 'SEED: <S>' where S is drawn uniformly at random per example. Keep a 'null' condition (no seed) and optionally a 'pause' condition for controls. • Inference: with seed-conditioning, use fresh unseen seeds; with null, use no prefix.
- Default hyperparameters (adapt per model and task, matching paper ranges): • Gemma 2B: batch (packed) ≈ 4; seq len: 32 (Sibling/Triangle), 2048 (Circle/Line). Max LR 5e-4 (Line: 5e-5). Cosine decay after 100-step warmup to 0.01×. Steps: 7.5k–15k (see paper table). λ (MTP weight): 0.5 (Sibling/Triangle), 0.75 (Circle/Line). • GPT-2 86M: batch 64, seq len 128, LR 1e-4, train to convergence for creativity within 20k–80k steps. • SEDD 90M: LR 1e-4, batch 64, 80k steps; default sampler settings.
- Sampling conditions to sweep: • Decoding: greedy, nucleus p=0.95; temperatures ∈ {0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0}; with/without top-k (k=50). • Prefix types: null, seed(L∈{2,4,10}), pause(10). • For seed-conditioned Transformers, include greedy decoding to test if seed alone induces diversity.
- Ablations: • Token order: train Sibling Discovery in reversed order (Γ,γ,γ′) and compare to sibling-first. • Dataset size scaling: multiply S by {1×,2×,4×,8×,16×,32×}; plot expected theoretical max creativity vs observed. • Task complexity: vary Triangle |V|∈{500,999}, deg∈{3,10}, tri∈{6,10,25}; Circle/Line N∈{7,9}, M∈{10,12,15}. • Seed length: L∈{0,2,4,10}. • Format sensitivity: Triangle edge-list vs node-list representation. • Model size: small (~86–90M) vs medium (~400M) for trend stability.
- Evaluation pipeline per checkpoint: • Generate T samples with fixed random seed for reproducibility per condition. • Compute coherence: - Sibling: check γ,γ′ share parent Γ inferred from learned in-weights edges approximated by training adjacency (acceptable proxy) or train a lightweight edge-estimator from training pairs. - Triangle: verify all three undirected edges are present in G; disallow triangles absent from G. - Circle/Line: reconstruct adjacency; check it resolves to a single Hamiltonian cycle/line consistent with degrees; derive permutation. • Compute memorization memS(s): membership in training set modulo canonicalization rules per task. • Compute diversity uniq count after canonicalization. • Algorithmic creativity: uniq(non-memorized coherent samples)/T. • Store breakdown: coherence rate, diversity, memorization rate, seed-vs-temp conditions.
- Summarization extension (optional): • Datasets: XSUM and CNN/DailyMail; fine-tune GPT-2 sizes for 1 epoch with NTP or MTP (λ=0.5). • For each doc, sample 5 generations; measure quality as average ROUGE (R-1,R-2,R-L); diversity as 1−Self-BLEU (BLEU-2). • Plot diversity vs ROUGE over training steps to compare NTP vs MTP at fixed quality.

## Results Interpretation

- Core comparisons: • Show algorithmic creativity (with 95% CIs) for NTP vs MTP vs SEDD across all four tasks; highlight large gains of MTP/diffusion, especially on discovery tasks. • Decompose creativity into diversity and memorization; attribute MTP gains largely to reduced memorization and improved coverage; attribute seed-conditioning gains primarily to diversity increases.
- Seed-conditioning vs temperature: • For Transformers, compare seed(L=10)+greedy vs null+temp in {0.5,1,2} with/without top-k. Emphasize cases where seed+greedy matches or beats temperature while maintaining coherence.
- Failure/success modes: • NTP: increased memorization and mode collapse under null prefix; improved but still suboptimal under reversed Sibling order; sensitive to Triangle formatting (node-based poor). • MTP: more robust diversity; sometimes optimization-sensitive for small models; still benefits from seed-conditioning in top-k regimes.
- Scaling and robustness: • Show that gaps persist across reasonable hyperparameter ranges; diminish with very large data as expected; lines/paths are more NTP-friendly than cycles/triangles.
- Theory-aligned insights: • Connect observed 'Clever Hans' shortcut in NTP to higher memorization; multi-token/diffusion better capture latent plan z; seed-conditioning likely helps by focusing on one latent plan per seed.
- Summarization extension: • For larger GPT models on XSUM, show slight diversity improvements at matched ROUGE under MTP; note weaker or inconsistent gains on CNN/DM and smaller models; seed-conditioning shows no clear effect on diversity for summarization.

## Report Writing

- Document datasets precisely: construction algorithms, formatting strings, canonicalization rules, and default hyperparameters; release scripts to regenerate data with fixed RNG seeds.
- Provide a reproducibility matrix listing: model (size), objective (NTP/MTP/SEDD), prefix (null/seed/pause), decoding (greedy/temp/top-k), and all metric outcomes.
- Include ablation figures: • Creativity vs objective (Fig 3/4 analogs). • Seed vs temperature (Fig 5/6 analogs). • Memorization breakdowns and diversity trajectories over training. • Token-order reversal (Sibling), format sensitivity (Triangle). • Data scaling curves with theoretical upper bounds for creativity and observed diversity.
- Summarization section (optional): diversity vs ROUGE plots for NTP vs MTP across model sizes; show seed-conditioning null results.
- Discuss limitations and future work: • Minimal tasks vs real-world generality, optimization sensitivity for small MTP models, diffusion seed-conditioning null effect, equivalence class choices in circle/line signatures. • Suggest next steps: alternative multi-token methods (lookahead attention, energy-based models), principled seed-to-latent mapping, and evaluating on richer creative domains.
- Provide a concise checklist: software versions, hardware, training wallclock, seeds; and release code/configs to replicate all figures end-to-end.

Source: MLReplicate Agent Laboratory task adapter (Apache-2.0). This adapter is one representation of the shared paper task; other systems have their own input formats.
